## Load data
Profile variables:
- IBS-ss total score
- depression total
- anxiety total (gad-2)
- catastrophizing total
- positive affect total ()
- parenting hassles (frequency)
- social support total
- family resilience
- num hh with pain (caregivers, biocaregivers, people who child spends time)
- eating meals together
- income to needs
- parent education (college vs less)
Outcome variables:
- parent protective responses
- child emotional functioning
Covariates:
- child age
- parent age
- first child
- child sex
- parent sex
```{r}
mplus <- read_csv("../analysis_data_2026-04-01.csv") %>% 
  dplyr::select(
    study_id,
    # covariates
    child_age,
    oldest_child,
    child_sex,
    parent_age,
    parent_sex,
    # profile vars
    income_to_needs,
    total_hh_pain,
    dpfreq_tot,
    phq_tot,
    gad_tot,
    pcs_tot,
    mspss_tot,
    total_ppp,
    pain_duration,
    panaspa,
    parent_college,
    parent_graddeg,
    num_caregivers_pain,
    num_biocare_pain,
    famresil_total,
    ibs_tot_re,
    fammeal_days,
    # outcome vars
    arcsp_tot,
    ql_efs
  )
```


# Clean data for Mplus
```{r}
# id: remove first 5 characters
mplus_clean <- mplus %>% 
  mutate(
    study_id = as.numeric(str_sub(study_id, 6))
  )

# binarize oldest child, childsex
mplus_clean <- mplus_clean %>% 
  mutate(
    oldest_child = ifelse(oldest_child=="Yes", 1, 0),
    child_female = ifelse(child_sex == "Female", 1, 0),
    parent_female = ifelse(parent_sex == "Female", 1, 0)
  )

# create fammeals categorical var where num is higher with increasing frequency of family meals
mplus_clean <- mplus_clean %>% 
  dplyr::select(
    -child_sex,
    -parent_sex
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate( # collapse into 3 categories since there's only 1% in 0 days cat
    fammeal_days_cat = case_when(
      fammeal_days == "0 days" ~ 1,
      fammeal_days == "1-3 days" ~ 1,
      fammeal_days == "4-6 days" ~ 2,
      fammeal_days == "Every day" ~ 3
    )
  )

# remove non-categorical fammeals var
mplus_clean <- mplus_clean %>% 
  dplyr::select(-fammeal_days)

mean_page <- mean(mplus_clean$parent_age, na.rm=TRUE)
# mean impute 2 missing parent ages (REACH271 and REACH375)
mplus_clean[mplus_clean$study_id == "271", "parent_age"] <- mean_page
mplus_clean[mplus_clean$study_id == "375", "parent_age"] <- mean_page


# change NA to -999
mplus_clean <- mplus_clean %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    across(everything(), ~ifelse(is.na(.), -999, .))
  )
```

```{r}
runModels(filefilter = ".*_mplus\\.inp$", showOutput=TRUE)
```

# Mplus analysis steps
1. Missing values estimated using FIML in LPA
2. Iterative model evaluation (1-5 or 6 profiles)
3. Evaluate models to identify fit and interpretability
4. Interpret retained model -- examine patterns of the profiles and weights of included variables in each profile 
5. Covariate analysis

# Step 3: Read in Mplus results and create comparison table of model fit stats to identify best-fitting model
```{r}
read_mplus_out <- function(file) {
  readLines(file, warn = FALSE)
}

# extract values of interest

# extract lowest log likelihood
extract_loglik <- function(x) {
  idx <- which(stringr::str_detect(x, "Final stage loglikelihood values"))
  
  if (length(idx) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  if (idx[1] + 2 > length(x)) return(NA_real_)
  
  target_line <- x[idx[1] + 2]
  
  as.numeric(stringr::str_extract(target_line, "-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?"))
}

extract_ic <- function(x, label) {
  as.numeric(
    stringr::str_match(
      x[stringr::str_detect(x, label)][1],
      "(-?[0-9\\.]+)$"
    )[,2]
  )
}

#aic  <- extract_ic(out, "Akaike")
#bic  <- extract_ic(out, "Bayesian")
#sabic <- extract_ic(out, "Sample-Size Adjusted")

extract_entropy <- function(x) {
  ent <- x[stringr::str_detect(x, "Entropy")]
  if (length(ent) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  as.numeric(stringr::str_extract(ent[1], "[0-9\\.]+$"))
}

extract_lmr <- function(x) {
  lmr <- which(stringr::str_detect(x, "LO-MENDELL-RUBIN ADJUSTED"))
  
  if (length(lmr) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  if (lmr[1] + 3 > length(x)) return(NA_real_)
  
  target_line <- x[lmr[1] + 3]
  
  as.numeric(stringr::str_extract(target_line, "[0-9\\.]+$"))
}

extract_blrt <- function(x) {
  blrt <- which(stringr::str_detect(x, "BOOTSTRAPPED LIKELIHOOD RATIO TEST"))
  
  if (length(blrt) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  if (blrt[1] + 3 > length(x)) return(NA_real_)
  
  target_line <- x[blrt[1] + 5]
  
  as.numeric(stringr::str_extract(target_line, "[0-9\\.]+$"))
}

extract_classes <- function(file) {
  as.integer(stringr::str_extract(basename(file), "\\d+"))
}

extract_enum_metrics <- function(file) {
  out <- read_mplus_out(file)

  tibble::tibble(
    classes = extract_classes(file),
    min_loglik  = extract_loglik(out),
    aic     = extract_ic(out, "Akaike"),
    bic     = extract_ic(out, "Bayesian"),
    sabic   = extract_ic(out, "Sample-Size Adjusted"),
    entropy = extract_entropy(out),
    lmr_p   = extract_lmr(out),
    blrt_p  = extract_blrt(out)
  )
}

out_files <- list.files(
  path = "../reach_neighborhood_parentfunctioning/final_lpa_models_forselection/",
  pattern = "\\mplus.out$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

reach_enum_table_final <- map_dfr(out_files, extract_enum_metrics) %>%
  arrange(classes)

reach_enum_table_final_formatted <- reach_enum_table_final
colnames(reach_enum_table_final_formatted) <- c("Classes", "Min. Log Likelihood", "AIC", "BIC", "SABIC", "Entropy", "LMR p-value", "Boot LMR p-value")

# generate word-compatible APA format table, export
library(rempsyc)
table1 <- nice_table(
  reach_enum_table_final_formatted,
  title = c("Table 1", "Fit Statistics for Models with 1-5 Subgroups"),
  note = ""
)

flextable::save_as_docx(table1, path = "tables/table1.docx")
```

# Step 4: Evaluate patterns of profiles

When SAVE=CPROBABILITIES is used in conjunction with
TYPE=MIXTURE in the ANALYSIS command, individual posterior
probabilities for each latent class are saved along with the other analysis
variables. In addition, a variable is saved that contains the most likely
class membership, that is, the class with the highest posterior probability
for each individual.
Last 4 columns are: posterior class probabilities (class 1 -x) and then last column: most likely class

## Extract estimated means for each class for profiles plot: 3-profile solution
From: https://garberadamc.github.io/project-site/mlca-replication
```{r}
# extract class probabilities
#dat <- read_table("LPA4.dat")
dat3 <- readr::read_table("LPA3_final.dat", 
                         col_names = c("parent_college", "fammeal_days_cat", "income_to_needs", "total_hh_pain", "dpfreq_tot", "phq_tot", "gad_tot", "pcs_tot", "mspss_tot", "panaspa", "famresil_total", "ibs_tot_re", "class1_prob", "class2_prob", "class3_prob", "class_assign", "study_id"))

lpa3_classprob <- dat3 %>% 
  dplyr::select(study_id, contains("class")) %>% 
  left_join(mplus_clean, by = "study_id")

lpa3_classprob %>%
  dplyr::select(-class_assign) %>% 
  pivot_longer(starts_with("class"),
               names_to = "class",
               values_to = "prob") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = class, y = prob)) +
  geom_violin()

lpa3_classprob %>% dplyr::count(class_assign)

# extract model-estimated means
lpa3profile_means <- output$reach_3profile_mplus.out$parameters$unstandardized %>% 
  filter(paramHeader== "Means") %>% 
  filter(LatentClass != "Categorical.Latent.Variables") %>% 
  dplyr::select(
    class = LatentClass,
    indicator=param,
    mean_model=est
  ) %>%  # rename indicators back to full var names
  mutate(
    indicator=case_when(
      indicator=="INCOME_TO_" ~ "income_to_needs",
      indicator=="TOTAL_HH_P" ~ "total_hh_pain",
      indicator=="DPFREQ_TOT" ~ "dpfreq_tot",
      indicator=="PHQ_TOT" ~ "phq_tot",
      indicator=="GAD_TOT" ~ "gad_tot",
      indicator=="PCS_TOT" ~ "pcs_tot",
      indicator=="MSPSS_TOT" ~ "mspss_tot",
      indicator=="PANASPA" ~ "panaspa",
      indicator=="FAMRESIL_T" ~ "famresil_total",
      indicator=="IBS_TOT_RE" ~ "ibs_tot_re"
    )
  )

# standardize the means for plotting
# compute reference means and SD from the raw data
ref_stats_3profiles <- mplus_clean %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~na_if(., -999))) %>% 
  summarise(across(
    c(income_to_needs, total_hh_pain, dpfreq_tot, phq_tot, gad_tot, pcs_tot, mspss_tot, panaspa, famresil_total, ibs_tot_re),
    list(mean = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
         sd   = ~ sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE))
  )) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = c("indicator", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "^(.*)_(mean|sd)$"
  ) %>% 
  rename(mean_data = mean,
         sd_data = sd)

# standardize the estimated means
plot_means_3profiles <- lpa3profile_means %>%
  left_join(ref_stats_3profiles, by = "indicator") %>%
  mutate(z_mean = (mean_model - mean_data) / sd_data)

# extract model estimated class sizes
c_size <- output$reach_3profile_mplus.out$class_counts$mostLikely

plot_means_3profiles <- plot_means_3profiles %>%
  mutate(class=as.numeric(class)) %>% 
  left_join(c_size, by = "class") 

plot_means_3profiles <- plot_means_3profiles %>% 
  mutate(pct = proportion*100)

class_labels_3pofiles <- plot_means_3profiles %>%
  distinct(class, pct) %>%          # one row per class
  arrange(class) %>%
  mutate(
    label = paste0(
      "Group ", class, " (", round(pct, 1), "%)"
    )
  )

label_vec_3profiles <- setNames(class_labels_3pofiles$label, class_labels_3pofiles$class)

plot_means_3profiles$indicator <- factor(
  plot_means_3profiles$indicator,
  levels = c("income_to_needs", "dpfreq_tot", "gad_tot", "phq_tot", "pcs_tot", "ibs_tot_re", "panaspa", "mspss_tot", "famresil_total", "total_hh_pain"),
  labels = c("Income-to-Needs", "Parenting Stress", "Anxiety", "Depression", "Catastrophizing", "IBS Symptoms", "Positive Affect", "Social Support", "Family Resilience", "Fam. Mem. w/Pain")
)

# paper figure version
ggplot(plot_means_3profiles, aes(indicator, z_mean, shape = as.factor(class), 
                    colour = as.factor(class), group=class, lty = as.factor(class))) +
  geom_point(size = 3) + geom_line() + 
  #scale_x_continuous("", breaks = 1:10) + 
  scale_y_continuous("Mean (standardized)") + 
  scale_colour_grey(
    labels = label_vec_3profiles
  ) +
  scale_shape_discrete(
    labels = label_vec_3profiles
  ) +
  scale_linetype_discrete(
    labels = label_vec_3profiles
  ) +
  xlab(NULL) +
  #theme_cowplot() +
  theme(text=element_text(family="Times New Roman", size=10),
        legend.key.width = unit(.5, "line"),
        legend.text = element_text(family="Times New Roman", size=10),
        legend.title = element_blank(), 
        legend.position = "top", 
        panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
                         panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
                         panel.border = element_rect(
                           color = "black",  
                           size = 0.5),
        panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
        plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))

ggsave("tables/figure1_pres.png", dpi=1000, width=6, height=4)

# grand rounds presentation version
ggplot(plot_means_3profiles, aes(indicator, z_mean, shape = as.factor(class), 
                    colour = as.factor(class), group=class, alpha=as.factor(class))) +
  geom_point(size = 3) + geom_line() + 
  #scale_x_continuous("", breaks = 1:10) + 
  scale_y_continuous("Mean (standardized)") +
```

### Step 4 Covariate Analysis: Try BCH 3-step approach
Most computationally complex, but simulation studies suggest its more robust than ANCOVA
Over ANCOVA, this method is recommend because it allows for the uncertainty of the profile assignment to remain in the model while also maintaining integrity of profiles with covariates added
From Mplus user manual: https://www.statmodel.com/examples/webnotes/webnote21.pdf

```{r}
# read the appropriate section of the output into results table in R
outcomes_3profile <- readModels("reach_3profile_mplus_covs_bch_step3.out")

# extract parameters
outcomes_3profile_regression <- outcomes_3profile$regression %>% 
  dplyr::select(lhs, rhs, est, se, pval, stdyx)
```

# Outcomes analysis with covariates: 3-profile solution
reach_3profile_mplus_covs_bch_step3_statmodel_covs_final.out:
- Emotional functioning: Overall chi-square significant
  - significant difference class 1 vs 2 (class 2 lower)
  - significant difference class 1 vs 3 (class 3 lower)
  - n.s. class 2 vs 3
- Parent protectiveness: chi-square n.s.
  - marginal difference class 1 vs 3, all others n.s.
- covariate differences across classes: n.s.
```{r}
# extract parameters from covariate analysis
# read mplus lpa model output into R
output_outcomes_3profile <- readModels("../reach_neighborhood_parentfunctioning/reach_3profile_mplus_covs_bch_step3_statmodel_covs_final.out")

# this automatic summary cannot extract entropy, but other values yes (though T11 values are diff from overall LMR p-value)
# Pull the full text output
```

# Code to convert 'thresholds' to probabilities
Mplus parameterizes binary indicators with thresholds on a latent response scale.
prob <- function(x) 1 / (1 + exp(-(-x)))
```{r}
prob <- function(x) 1 / (1 + exp(-(-x)))

prob(1.49) # class 1 college prob = .18
prob(-15) # class 2 college prob = .99
prob (-1.76) # class 3 college prob = .85
prob(1.29) # class 4 college prob = .22
```

```{r}
# anova and lsd for continuous variables

  contdemovars,
  ~ aov(reformulate("class_assign", response = .x), data = lpa3_classprob_demos) %>%
      tidy() %>%
      mutate(outcome = .x)
)

# chi-square for counts for categorical variables
# uses Fisher's exact test for cases with sparse categories (and simulated p-value)
catdemovars <- c("relationchild", "parent_sex", "pgender", "parent_race_nih", "parent_eth", "child_sex", "child_eth", "child_race_nih", "parent_work", "notwork_reason", "relationstatus", "oldest_child", "child_outsidecare")

chisq_results <- map_dfr(catdemovars, function(v) {

  tab <- table(lpa3_classprob_demos$class_assign, lpa3_classprob_demos[[v]])

  chisq_obj <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tab))

  if(any(chisq_obj$expected < 5)) {

    test <- fisher.test(
      tab,
      simulate.p.value = TRUE,
      B = 10000
    )

    method <- "fisher_simulated"

  } else {

    test <- chisq_obj
    method <- "chisq"
  }

  broom::tidy(test) %>%
    mutate(
      variable = v,
      method_used = method
    )
})
```

# Revisions in response to R1 at JoP
## Effect size of mean separation between classes
cohen's d = 0.8 (large effect)
cohen's d = 0.5 (medium effect)
cohen's d = 0.2 (small effect)
Convert SEs from Mplus to SD: SE * sqrt(group N)
Pooled standard deviation: sqrt[(n1-1)*s1^2 + (n2-1)*s2^2/(n1+n2-2)]
```{r}

# continuous variables: mean difference / (pooled sd)

model_results_3profile <- readxl::read_xlsx("final_bch_cov_analysis/mplus_output_3profile_groupdiffs.xlsx")

library(dplyr)

#---------------------------------------
# Function to calculate pooled SD and d
#---------------------------------------
calc_d <- function(n1, mean1, se1,
                   n2, mean2, se2){

  sd1 <- se1 * sqrt(n1)
  sd2 <- se2 * sqrt(n2)

  pooled_sd <- sqrt(
    (((n1 - 1) * sd1^2) +
       (n2 - 1) * sd2^2) /
      (n1 + n2 - 2)
  )

  d <- (mean1 - mean2) / pooled_sd

  c(sd1 = sd1,
    sd2 = sd2,
    pooled_sd = pooled_sd,
    d = d)
}

#---------------------------------------
# Calculate effect sizes for every row
#---------------------------------------

effect_sizes <-
  model_results_3profile %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(

    ## Group 1 vs Group 2
    g1_g2 = list(calc_d(g1_n, g1_mean, g1_se,
                        g2_n, g2_mean, g2_se)),

    ## Group 1 vs Group 3
    g1_g3 = list(calc_d(g1_n, g1_mean, g1_se,
                        g3_n, g3_mean, g3_se)),

    ## Group 2 vs Group 3
    g2_g3 = list(calc_d(g2_n, g2_mean, g2_se,
                        g3_n, g3_mean, g3_se))
  ) %>%
  mutate(

    d_g1_g2 = g1_g2["d"],
    d_g1_g3 = g1_g3["d"],
    d_g2_g3 = g2_g3["d"],

    pooledsd_g1_g2 = g1_g2["pooled_sd"],
    pooledsd_g1_g3 = g1_g3["pooled_sd"],
    pooledsd_g2_g3 = g2_g3["pooled_sd"]

  ) %>%
  select(-g1_g2, -g1_g3, -g2_g3) %>%
  ungroup()

# binary variables: cox transformation on odds ratio
prop_to_d <- function(p1, p2){

  OR <- (p2/(1-p2)) / (p1/(1-p1))
  log(OR) * sqrt(3) / pi
}

# group 1 vs group 2 education
prop_to_d(0.17, 0.99) 

# group 1 vs group 3 education
prop_to_d(0.17, 0.03) 

# group 2 vs group 3 education
prop_to_d(0.03, 0.99) 

# multicategorical variable (family meal frequency): cramer's v
lpa3_classprob_g12 <- lpa3_classprob %>% dplyr::filter(class_assign != 3)
lpa3_classprob_g13 <- lpa3_classprob %>% dplyr::filter(class_assign != 2)
lpa3_classprob_g23 <- lpa3_classprob %>% dplyr::filter(class_assign != 1)

rstatix::cramer_v(lpa3_classprob_g12$class_assign, lpa3_classprob_g12$fammeal_days_cat) # 0.08
rstatix::cramer_v(lpa3_classprob_g13$class_assign, lpa3_classprob_g13$fammeal_days_cat) # 0.13
rstatix::cramer_v(lpa3_classprob_g23$class_assign, lpa3_classprob_g23$fammeal_days_cat) # 0.06
```

```{r}
# code from graph in original manuscript -- reproduced below

# standardize the means for plotting
# compute reference means and SD from the raw data
ref_stats_3profiles <- mplus_clean %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~na_if(., -999))) %>% 
  summarise(across(
    c(income_to_needs, total_hh_pain, dpfreq_tot, phq_tot, gad_tot, pcs_tot, mspss_tot, panaspa, famresil_total, ibs_tot_re),
    list(mean = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
         sd   = ~ sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE))
  )) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = c("indicator", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "^(.*)_(mean|sd)$"
  ) %>% 
  rename(mean_data = mean,
         sd_data = sd)

# standardize the estimated means
# NEW: add sds to SE dataframe
# standardize the SEs by dividing by the SD
plot_3profiles <- lpa3profile_means %>%
  left_join(ref_stats_3profiles, by = "indicator") %>%
  mutate(z_mean = (mean_model - mean_data) / sd_data) %>% 
  left_join(lpa3profile_se, by = c("class", "indicator")) %>%
  mutate(z_se = (se_model) / sd_data,
         z_upper = z_mean + z_se,
         z_lower = z_mean - z_se)
```

```{r}
abpain_qs_dx %>% dplyr::count(bowel_habit_sat <50 & other_gi_sx==1) %>% mutate(perc = n / sum(n)) # 39 people didn't rate their bowel dissatisfaction as at least 50, of those, 30 said 'yes' to other symptoms (77%)
```
Results (ended up not using):

We could do a symptom sub-analysis with IBS-SS for bowel habit symptoms to say something like “x% of participants reported significant bowel habit symptoms, supporting the sample characterization as predominantly IBS patients”? Or is this not necessary?
 
IBS-SS: mean = 228 (94); Range: 0 – 460
•	The person who scored 0 on IBS symptoms met ROME IV IBS criteria on enrollment
•	Of the 8 people in the “little to no symptom severity” category (average score less than 25 out of 100 for severeity of ab pain, frequency of ab pain, severeity of ab bloating, dissatisfaction with bowel habits, interference with quality of life) 6 said “yes” to “experiencing irritable bowel or abdominal pain at least once a week in the past 3 months”, 6 said “yes” to “experiencing any other digestive problems such as reflux, constipation, diarrhea, or bloating, at least once a week in the past 3 months?”, all said “yes” to at least one of those two questions, and 4 said yes to both
Maximum score someone could get if they only had abdominal pain: 300 (so everyone with ‘severe’ symptoms has to have at least some other symptoms)
27% of potential participants who were sent ROME on screening (i.e., because they did not have a diagnosis in the last 5 years) were excluded due to not meeting criteria 
Of the people who were included based on a recent diagnosis:
•	IBS symptom severity: 4% little to no symptom severity, 28% mild IBS symptoms, 47% moderate IBS symptoms, 19% severe IBS symtpoms, 2% did not complete
•	76% rated dissatisfaction with bowel habits as at least 50 out of 100 (most dissatisfaction)
o	Of the people who rated their dissatisfaction as less than 50, 77% said ‘yes’ to “experiencing any other digestive problems such as reflux, constipation, diarrhea, or bloating, at least once a week in the past 3 months” 
•	87% said “yes” to “experiencing any other digestive problems such as reflux, constipation, diarrhea, or bloating, at least once a week in the past 3 months?”
o	Of the people who said “no” to the other symptoms question, 
	57% rated disssatisfaction with bowel habits as at least 50 out 100 (most dissatisfaction)
	76% rated disssatisfaction with bowel habits as at least 25 out of 100
So, 5.5% of those were not screened with ROME criteria said pretty satisfied with bowels + ‘no’ to other sytmpoms

```{r}
)
```
